cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a colourful appliqué felt tent-cloth (shyrdak) with classic Central Asian nomadic motifs (ram's-horn kochkor muyuz, rosettes, stylised flowers/butterflies) — a felt craft shared across the Central Asian steppe and plausible for Kazakh material culture even if the embroidered place-name points to Kyrgyzstan; neighbouring nomadic groups' felt work cannot be reliably distinguished.

reattribution.reason: This is a shyrdak-style felt tent-cloth with typical ram's-horn (kochkor muyuz) border motifs, appliquéd floral and butterfly designs, matching the described Kyrgyz felt textile tradition (with Kyrgyz-language embroidery reference to Ат-Башы).

physical.title: tent-cloth
physical.summary: Tent-cloth; made of "shyrdak" felt; rectangle of black felt for back; front red with black border around edge with alternating multicoloured W shapes (ram's horn [kochkor muyuz]) and white circles with multicoloured centres; two multicoloured butterflies and flower on blue background at centre, multicoloured flowers in each corner; "АТ БАШЫ РАИРНҮ 08 АҮА-КАИЫНДЫ АИЫЛЫ АПЫБЕКОВА ЊАНЫП 1938 - ЊЫА" embroidered in black along one border.
